geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Draw {5/2} and {7/3} star polygons in line art.

Goal: I can find angle measures of regular polygons and star polygons.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A regular polygon is both equilateral and equiangular. Each interior angle of a regular n-gon is (n − 2)180/n and each exterior angle is 360/n. A regular pentagon has interior angles of 108 degrees.

A star polygon {n/k} joins every kth of n equally spaced points on a circle. For 1≤k<n/2 and a single circuit with gcd(n,k)=1, each vertex angle is 180 − 360k/n degrees. If gcd(n,k)>1, the drawing is a compound of gcd(n,k) cycles, not one n-pointed star. So {5/2} has 36 degree points and {7/3} has 180 − 1080/7, about 25.7 degrees.

The regular pentagon can be constructed with compass and straightedge, because its diagonal to side ratio is the golden ratio (1 + √5)/2.
